transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from the NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Russia fired a ballistic missile on the hometown of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
The attack killed a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic.
More than 50 others were injured.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports from Kyiv.
The attack targeted the densely populated downtown area of the southern town of Krivirezh.
Local official Alexander Vilkul called it a tragic evening and night for our city,
as Russian terrorists have launched another series of criminal attacks.
Two ballistic missiles were launched at an area near a popular restaurant,
followed by a swarm of Shahed-type drones that struck first responders
in what's known as a double-tap strike.
The seven-year-old died in the hospital after sustaining trauma to his head,
and a three- and four-year-old were among the wounded.
Meanwhile, in a call to European leaders after his meeting with Russia's president in China Thursday,
President Trump told them Vladimir Putin is serious about negotiating a peace deal.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv.
About five million people lost SNAP food benefits over the past year.
NPR's Juliana Kim reports in San Diego social service workers have been working overtime to run a food pantry.
These county employees typically help San Diego residents apply for food assistance.
But lately, on the weekends, they've been simply handing out free food.
Nina Olivas oversees the call center where people dial in and ask about safety net programs.
She says this was one way to make sure people are getting help whether or not they still qualify for SNAP.
We are not ending the call with nothing.
There's something that we can do for each customer.
And so we're really just trying to focus on that, even though the time has been so difficult.
Across the U.S., SNAP roles have been shrinking as federal changes to the program take effect.
That includes imposing work requirements on more people and banning food benefits to most refugees and asylum seekers.
Juliana Kim, NPR News.
President Trump says there may be a connection between a drop in crude oil prices and the midterm elections.
Crude oil prices have plummeted right since the end of the election.
I wonder how that happened.
Crude oil is down 20 percent since the start of November.
And now it's down to close to 80 dollars a barrel.
And one of the largest drops, they say, in the history of oil, it's the biggest drop on record.
U.S. crude futures settled Friday at just under 84 dollars a barrel.
That's down about 13 percent from Election Day.
There have been much steeper drops, including a nearly 80 percent slide in the second half of 2008.
Stocks fell on Wall Street this week.
The decline was led by a sell-off in companies tied to artificial intelligence.
This is NPR News.
A second federal judge has blocked President Trump's plan to build a memorial arch in the nation's capital.
Lawyers challenging the project say Friday's ruling in Virginia will keep construction on hold while several lawsuits play out.
Two days earlier, a federal judge in Washington extended a temporary order barring the administration from breaking ground.
A Virginia county board sued over the project, saying it would make traffic worse and put public safety at risk.
The Kansas City Chiefs' wheelchair football team is one game away from a three-peat.
As Frank Morris of member station KCUR reports, the Chiefs play for their third consecutive championship today against their arch rival, the wheelchair Chicago Bears.
The Chiefs have been dominant in the 15-member USA Wheelchair Football League since the beginning.
They played in all five championship games, beating the wheelchair Bears in the last two.
League commissioner Carolyn Lee says it's always a grudge match.
They are very closely matched.
It's a really unique rivalry here, and it's really going to be a fun game.
The Chiefs have the home field advantage, but the wheelchair Bears have a new weapon.
A former Chiefs standout who moved for work and signed on with the Bears.
For NPR News, I'm Frank Morris in Kansas City.
New York City Mayor Zoran Mamdani plans to close the Rikers Island jail complex by 2032.
The city is expected to miss its legal deadline to close Rikers and replace it with four smaller jails by 2027.
A judge has appointed an outside manager to address overcrowding and violence at the complex.
This is NPR.
